source.description: One approved eight-panel felt-tip marker contact sheet plus one scoped raster repair sheet for the five defective pencil construction frames; the approved ink, color, and finished masters remain unchanged.
source.notes: Repair Steps 1-5 so the same right-facing swimming axolotl grows from sparse proportion masses into a connected silhouette, four limbs plus three gills, facial features, and secondary accents. Keep approved Steps 6-7 and the finished image byte-identical. The superseded front-loaded pencil panels remain private for comparison.

process_strategy: Use the Sketcha-style stage grammar explicitly: sparse gesture and proportion masses, connected head-body-tail silhouette, rough limbs and gills, face, secondary accents, ink, color, then finish. Step 1 must not work as a faint coloring-book version of the final; every early frame has a distinct visible job and a must-not-show boundary.

construction_contract.temporary_guides: Pale head and body ellipses, one center axis, one tail gesture, and tiny attachment ticks may soften later; the pose, scale, proportions, and attachment locations they establish must persist.
construction_contract.step_1_boundary: Show only primitive masses and gesture marks. No connected outside silhouette, appendage envelopes, face, spots, bubbles, highlights, shadow, ink, or color.
construction_contract.step_2_boundary: Connect the major head-body-tail masses into a loose silhouette while keeping limbs and gills as single-line routes. No feet, gill leaves, face, spots, bubbles, highlights, shadow, ink, or color.
construction_contract.step_3_boundary: Add rough limb and gill envelopes to the established silhouette. No eye, pupil, mouth, cheek hatches, dorsal spots, bubbles, highlights, water shadow, ink, or color.

final_elements.name: right-facing swimming gesture with rounded head and tapered body proportion masses
final_elements.description: One pale head ellipse, one long body mass, and one sweeping tail axis establish the finished right-facing pose, crop, scale, and major proportions without tracing the final contour.

final_elements.name: rough rounded head tapered body and broad curling tail-fin silhouette
final_elements.description: Loose handmade contours turn the map into one right-facing swimming axolotl with a wide head, tapered torso, and broad tail fin curling behind it.

final_elements.name: exactly four small limbs and exactly three external gill stalks
final_elements.description: Two near and two smaller far limb envelopes fit the swimming body while three simple external gill envelopes fan behind the head; their toe splits and feathery edges are refined one stage later.

final_elements.name: one oversized upward-looking eye one diamond mouth three cheek hatches and tail seam
final_elements.description: One large round eye with its pupil high in the socket, a tiny open diamond mouth, three short cheek hatches, and one tail-fin seam create a surprised swimming expression unlike recent two-eye side-eye characters.

final_elements.name: two dorsal spots three bubbles two highlights and one broken water shadow
final_elements.description: Exactly two rounded dorsal spots, three separate bubbles, two open-paper highlights, and one broken teal water-shadow mark complete the pre-ink drawing.

final_elements.name: full imperfect black structural ink
final_elements.description: Thick handmade black felt-tip traces only the established axolotl, four limbs, three gills, expression, spots, bubbles, highlights, tail seam, and water-shadow mark.

final_elements.name: coral raspberry navy and teal marker fills
final_elements.description: Coral pink fills the established body, raspberry fills the three gill stalks, deep navy fills the eye mouth and spots, and teal fills the three bubbles and broken shadow while two highlights remain open paper.

overlap_reservations.background_lines_stop_before: The broad tail fin begins only at its reserved body seam, and the body contour stops at all four limb attachments instead of running through them.

overlap_reservations.background_lines_stop_before: Tiny pale attachment ticks reserve the four limb and three gill junctions; Step 2's body contour stops at those junctions so Step 3 can add appendage envelopes without erasing keeper lines.

rejection_checks: Keep one right-facing swimming axolotl, one rounded head, one tapered body, one broad curling tail fin, four limbs, three gill stalks, one eye, one mouth, one crop, and one scale in all eight panels.
Keep exactly four limbs, exactly three visible gill stalks, exactly two dorsal spots, exactly three bubbles, three cheek hatches, and two highlights after those elements appear.
The head-body-tail curve, limb order, gill fan, pupil direction, mouth shape, spots, bubbles, highlights, and water-shadow footprint may not drift between panels.

Do not add a second eye, second character, extra limb, extra gill, extra spot, extra bubble, plant, castle, readable text, sticker outline, badge frame, label, arrow, number, signature, watermark, or decorative border.
The final panel may not introduce an anatomy contour, limb, gill, facial feature, spot, bubble, highlight, shadow shape, ink boundary, or color area.
The finish must retain visible felt-tip streaks and imperfect handmade edges rather than vector-clean clip art, glossy AI poster art, digital gradients, or rasterized vector drawing.
